Temperature-0, logprob-level diff against the live Kimi API, controlling for MoE routing noise (K2 is confirmed 1T-param/32B-active, 384-expert MoE — a known source of batch-dependent nondeterminism independent of caching). Protocol: (1) Noise floor: send an identical >256-token prompt with a randomized nonce suffix N=20 times, temperature=0, logprobs=true, top_logprobs=5, each call engineered to be a guaranteed cache miss (verify usage.cached_tokens==0 on every trial, discard any trial where it isn't); record per-token logprob variance across the 20 miss-only replies as the baseline. (2) Treatment: send one fixed >256-token prefix as a guaranteed miss, then N=20 follow-up calls reusing that exact prefix (verify usage.cached_tokens>0 on every trial, discard/retry any that come back 0) and diff the per-token logprobs of the shared-prefix continuation against the step-1 noise-floor *distribution*, not a single miss sample — single-sample text-only diffing can't distinguish "no divergence" from "divergence too small to flip the argmax." (3) Repeat straddling the 256-token cliff at exactly 250 and 260 tokens (fixed, tokenizer-counted) to test the boundary itself. (4) Re-run step 2 twice, once with the optional prompt_cache_key field set to a fixed value and once omitted, since its presence in the request schema (confirmed 2026-08-30, not previously noted in this entry) means routing may otherwise land hit/miss calls on different backend replicas, confounding cache-identity with replica-identity. Verdict rule: PASS_REPLAY if hit-trial logprob divergence is statistically indistinguishable from the miss-only noise floor across all three boundary conditions; FAIL if hit trials show a divergence distribution shifted measurably beyond that floor. Requires a Kimi API key, which this project does not hold as of 2026-08-30.
